explanations.explanation: That's the one, friend. Moses says that if Israel faithfully obeys the voice of the LORD their God, He "will set you high above all the nations of the earth." (Deuteronomy 28:1) Notice that little word "if" leading the way. It's the hinge the whole promise swings on.

Walls are a nice thought, baker, but Moses never mentions them here. He says the LORD will set Israel "high above all the nations of the earth." (Deuteronomy 28:1) The promise is about being set high, and nothing in the verse says anything about walls.

I see why that sounds right, but Moses doesn't say Israel will be far from anybody. He says the LORD "will set you high above all the nations of the earth." (Deuteronomy 28:1) Above is a place, and far away is a different place. The verse only gives us above.

explanations.answer: In the city and in the country
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker! Moses says, "You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the country." (Deuteronomy 28:3) Downtown or out in the fields, the blessing is there. That's about as wide as a list can get.

explanations.answer: In the temple and in the palace
explanations.explanation: Those sound fancy, friend, but they aren't on Moses' list. He says, "You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the country." (Deuteronomy 28:3) The blessing is for everyday places, which I like. Nobody needs a palace to be covered.

explanations.answer: In the desert and by the sea
explanations.explanation: Good scenery, but that's not what Moses says. He says, "You will be blessed in the city and blessed in the country." (Deuteronomy 28:3) City and country, that's the pair. I'm sure the desert and the sea are lovely, but they didn't make the list.

True! Moses says, "The fruit of your womb will be blessed, as well as the produce of your land and the offspring of your livestock—the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks." (Deuteronomy 28:4) Children, crops, calves and lambs, all of it gets named. Moses doesn't skip anybody on this list.

This one is true, baker. Moses says, "The fruit of your womb will be blessed, as well as the produce of your land and the offspring of your livestock—the calves of your herds and the lambs of your flocks." (Deuteronomy 28:4) So the children, the crops, the calves and the lambs are all in there. It's a long list, so it's easy to doubt something that big.

The kneading bowl, friend! Moses says, "Your basket and kneading bowl will be blessed." (Deuteronomy 28:5) A kneading bowl is where dough gets worked, so you can guess I felt that one personally. I may have wiped a happy tear off my mustache.

A pot is a fair guess, baker, but it isn't the one Moses names. He says, "Your basket and kneading bowl will be blessed." (Deuteronomy 28:5) The kneading bowl is where the dough gets worked. That's the answer.

Water jars matter, friend, but Moses doesn't mention one here. He says, "Your basket and kneading bowl will be blessed." (Deuteronomy 28:5) The kneading bowl is the one that gets named. Dough people, we notice these things.

Moses doesn't say that, baker. He says, "You will be blessed when you come in and blessed when you go out." (Deuteronomy 28:6) There's no warning tucked into the going out. The blessing covers both ends of the door.
False is right! Moses says, "You will be blessed when you come in and blessed when you go out." (Deuteronomy 28:6) No warning, no fine print about leaving. Coming in and going out are both covered.
Defeated is the word, friend. Moses says, "The LORD will cause the enemies who rise up against you to be defeated before you." (Deuteronomy 28:7) Notice who does the causing. It's the LORD.

Delayed sounds like a bus schedule, baker, not what Moses says. He says the LORD will cause the enemies who rise up against Israel "to be defeated before you." (Deuteronomy 28:7) Defeated is much stronger than a delay. The enemies don't get a later start time, they lose.

Pardoned is a kind word, friend, but it's not in this verse. Moses says the LORD will cause the enemies who rise up against Israel "to be defeated before you." (Deuteronomy 28:7) Defeated is the word he uses. Nobody gets a pardon slip in this one.

Holy, baker! Moses says, "The LORD will establish you as His holy people, just as He has sworn to you, if you keep the commandments of the LORD your God and walk in His ways." (Deuteronomy 28:9) That goes deeper than full barns. It's about who they belong to.

Mighty sounds impressive, friend, but that's not the word. Moses says, "The LORD will establish you as His holy people, just as He has sworn to you…" (Deuteronomy 28:9) Holy is about belonging to Him. That's bigger than being strong.

I get it, baker, with all those barns you'd expect money to come next. But Moses says, "The LORD will establish you as His holy people, just as He has sworn to you…" (Deuteronomy 28:9) Holy is the word. Moses goes bigger than barns here.

explanations.answer: They'll stand in awe of them
explanations.explanation: That's it, friend. Moses says, "Then all the peoples of the earth will see that you are called by the name of the LORD, and they will stand in awe of you." (Deuteronomy 28:10) They see the LORD's name on Israel, and awe is what follows.

Not quite, baker. Moses says the peoples of the earth "will see that you are called by the name of the LORD, and they will stand in awe of you." (Deuteronomy 28:10) Awe is the opposite of turning away. They look, and they're impressed.

Copying is a fair guess, friend, but Moses doesn't say it. He says the peoples of the earth "will see that you are called by the name of the LORD, and they will stand in awe of you." (Deuteronomy 28:10) The verse stops at awe. It doesn't go on to say what they do next.

Rain, baker! Moses says, "The LORD will open the heavens, His abundant storehouse, to send rain on your land in season…" (Deuteronomy 28:12) Rain in season means the right water at the right time. Any farmer would call that a good day.

Manna is a good thought, friend, since God did send it. But here Moses says, "The LORD will open the heavens, His abundant storehouse, to send rain on your land in season…" (Deuteronomy 28:12) Rain is what comes out of this storehouse. The manna story belongs somewhere else.

Sunshine is lovely, baker, but that's not what Moses says. He says, "The LORD will open the heavens, His abundant storehouse, to send rain on your land in season…" (Deuteronomy 28:12) Rain is what comes out of the storehouse. The crops get what the verse names.

That one's flipped, friend. Moses says, "You will lend to many nations, but borrow from none." (Deuteronomy 28:12) Israel lends to many and borrows from none. It's the other direction from what the question says.

False, baker! Moses says, "You will lend to many nations, but borrow from none." (Deuteronomy 28:12) Lending to many and borrowing from none, that's the promise. The question had the direction backwards.

explanations.answer: The head and not the tail
explanations.explanation: The head, friend! Moses says, "The LORD will make you the head and not the tail…" (Deuteronomy 28:13) The head leads and the tail follows. That's the picture Moses paints.

explanations.answer: The hands and not the feet
explanations.explanation: Close on body parts, baker, but that's not the picture. Moses says, "The LORD will make you the head and not the tail…" (Deuteronomy 28:13) It's the head and the tail. Hands and feet didn't make the verse.

explanations.answer: The eyes and not the ears
explanations.explanation: Good try, friend, but those two aren't in the verse. Moses says, "The LORD will make you the head and not the tail…" (Deuteronomy 28:13) The head and the tail are his picture. Eyes and ears will have to wait for another passage.

explanations.answer: Turn aside to the right or the left
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. Moses says, "Do not turn aside to the right or to the left from any of the words I command you today…" (Deuteronomy 28:14) Stay on the path. No wandering off to either side.

explanations.answer: Share the words with other nations
explanations.explanation: That's not what Moses says, friend. He says, "Do not turn aside to the right or to the left from any of the words I command you today…" (Deuteronomy 28:14) The warning is about turning aside from the words. Sharing them isn't mentioned here.

Nice guess, baker, but the priests don't come up in this warning. Moses says, "Do not turn aside to the right or to the left from any of the words I command you today…" (Deuteronomy 28:14) It's about staying on the path. No left turns and no right turns.

True, friend. Moses finishes the warning with "…and do not go after other gods to serve them." (Deuteronomy 28:14) That's how this part of his speech ends. It goes right back to obeying the LORD alone.

That one's true, baker. Moses finishes the warning with "…and do not go after other gods to serve them." (Deuteronomy 28:14) It's the very last line of the passage. Easy to miss when you're still thinking about all those blessings.
